tier_reason: EMQ (vendor of the competing EMQX broker) ran its own Open MQTT Benchmark Suite with the commercial XMeter tool; emqx/mqttbs holds only README prose, results pages and images, with no scripts or broker configs, and the CPU model is not stated, so not reproducible and not an independent suite: tier C. No peer-reviewed VerneMQ-vs-Mosquitto win could be opened (MDPI Energies 2021 Mishra et al. seen only as search snippets without results).

corrections.claimed_speedup: Sustains the 50k:50k msg/s offered load while Mosquitto 2.0.15 stabilises at 37,300/s for both pub and sub (about 1.34x higher sustained rate, derived from page data); 1M-connection (5k cps) scenario average connection latency 2.47 ms against Mosquitto 5.74 ms (about 2.3x lower, derived from page data; p50 2 ms for both). Latency is the opposite in the 50K:50K run: 2136.62 ms average pub-to-sub for VerneMQ against 353.82 ms for Mosquitto and 1.58 ms for EMQX. Against EMQX 4.4.16 VerneMQ loses in every scenario (1M connections: 2.47 ms vs EMQX 2.4 ms).
corrections.caveats: Weak, mixed evidence; recorded because it is the only numeric head-to-head against a listed baseline that could be opened. (1) Vendor-run: EMQ sells EMQX, a competing broker, and runs the suite itself; XMeter is the load generator, the emqx/mqttbs repo holds only prose scenario definitions (no scripts), broker configurations are not published except Mosquitto persistence disabled, and the CPU model is not stated, so not reproducible (tier C). (2) The win over Mosquitto is narrow: VerneMQ only sustains the target rate, while its latency is far worse (avg 2136.62 ms vs 353.82 ms; p50 467 vs 361 ms; p99 16,500 vs 417 ms). In the 250K fan-out QoS 1 scenario both stall near 80k/s (VerneMQ 80k, Mosquitto 81k; avg latency 11,802.11 vs 12,240.83 ms); in the 50K fan-in shared-subscription scenario VerneMQ collapses (pub 7.6k, sub 3.5k, avg 116,888.61 ms) while Mosquitto reaches pub 50k, sub 40k (12,723.07 ms). In the basic set Mosquitto has lower average latency (0.25 vs 0.4 ms point-to-point, 5.73 vs 21.55 ms fan-out, 0.20 vs 0.34 ms fan-in, 0.6 vs 0.89 ms for 10K connections). The 1M-connection latency edge over Mosquitto is 2.47 vs 5.74 ms average with equal p50 (2 ms). (3) Old versions: VerneMQ 1.12.6.2 and EMQX 4.4.16 from the 2023 post; current VerneMQ is 2.2.x. (4) The repo README has only qualitative claims (high-performance, low latency), no numbers, and no benchmark is linked from the repo page. (5) Independent studies seen only as WebSearch snippets because mdpi.com, arxiv.org and koziolek.de are blocked from this container: Koziolek 2020 edge-gateway study reports maximum sustainable throughput VerneMQ 10K msg/s, EMQX 28K, HiveMQ 8K (no Mosquitto or RabbitMQ); the MDPI Energies 2021 stress-test paper is reported to put VerneMQ 1.11.0 first on QoS 1 latency in its cloud tests (copies disagree, unverified). A small third-party suite (lkskrt/mqtt-broker-benchmark) lists VerneMQ as considered but has no VerneMQ results. No number against RabbitMQ MQTT plugin was found. (6) Domain/category corrected from the Haiku guess (other-languages / concurrency-runtimes) to storage-and-data / message-queues-logs, where the Mosquitto wave-6 entry already sits. (7) Verifier addendum: the throughput edge is a multi-core vs single-threaded design difference, not a faster per-core path. In the 50K:50K run Mosquitto used 6% average CPU of 16 vCPU (about one core) and 318M average memory, while VerneMQ used 90% average CPU and 6.02G average memory; the 50k/s figure is the offered-load target, so VerneMQ's ceiling was not measured. In the 1M-connection run VerneMQ's memory never stabilised (18 GB at 1M connections, rising to 22.4 GB by the end of the 30-minute test) against 1G for Mosquitto. (8) EMQ's own C broker NanoMQ 0.17.0, also in the post, reaches 50k:50k at 91 ms average latency with 30% CPU, so VerneMQ is not the strongest alternative to Mosquitto on this page. (9) Mosquitto's sustained rate is 37,300/s per the page prose (table shows 37k:37k).

notes: All quoted numbers match the emqx/blog page (50K:50K rates and latencies, p50/p99, fan-out, fan-in, 1M-connection rows, versions VerneMQ 1.12.6.2, Mosquitto 2.0.15, EMQX 4.4.16). Metadata checked on github.com: Apache-2.0, 3.6k stars, 432 forks, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-10-22 (after this prompt's 2026-10-11 date, so active). Win over Mosquitto is narrow and comes from using all 16 cores; caveats extended with CPU/memory and NanoMQ context.
